label: More and less ontologically true: For this reading, x is more true than y in the relevant respect…
term: more and less ontologically true (quarta-via comparative reading)
definition: For this reading, x is more true than y in the relevant respect when x more fully realizes the intelligible nature or form under consideration: the comparison is of realization of that form, hence of intelligibility grounded in actuality. It is not a comparison of two sentences’ accuracy, how many observers agree, or an observer’s certainty. The relevant form and comparative must be supplied by an interpretation of the things compared; no numerical measure or total comparability of all kinds is stipulated.
note: An explicit comparative gloss adopted for #211, motivated by q.16’s conformity/intelligibility account and q.2’s approach-to-a-maximum language. These passages do not themselves define this comparative relation, so it is not attributed to them as a separate sourced theorem. In Lean, MoreIn verum remains primitive: neither this gloss, existence of an exemplary intellect, nor an equality of the verum and esse comparisons is an added axiom or definition. Instantiating those parameters with a fully sourced conformity/comparison model and proving that it satisfies the root-path premises remains a further formalization obligation. Typed parameter location: the MoreIn : Respect → Being → Being → Prop and verum : Respect inputs to GradesFoundInThingsReading; MoreIn verum is their selected instance. The linked declaration is only a usage/constraining premise asserting some verum comparisons, not a definition implementing the conformity gloss. The intended comparative interpretation remains OPEN; a separately encoded candidate does not automatically identify these arbitrary parameters with that candidate.
